rigtune.report.button.tooltip: Opens a new GitHub issue in your browser, after you confirm the link, with your versions and hardware filled in. The full report is copied to your clipboard to paste into it. Nothing is posted until you submit the issue on GitHub.
rigtune.report.copied: Copied the full report (%s characters): paste it into the GitHub issue.
rigtune.screen.copy_report.tooltip: Copies a Markdown summary of your hardware and these suggestions, for Discord or a bug report. No file paths or user names.
rigtune.screen.header.modrinth_off: Modrinth off in settings: add and update mods in your launcher
rigtune.screen.header.network_off: Offline (network off in settings): add and update mods in your launcher
rigtune.screen.undo_all.tooltip: Revert every change RigTune has made. You see the full list before anything changes.
rigtune.screen.undo_last.tooltip: Revert RigTune's most recent Apply. You see exactly what changes before anything happens.
rigtune.settings.battery_offer.tooltip: On a laptop: when you unplug, RigTune offers to switch to the Battery profile, and when you plug back in, to switch back. It never switches by itself. "Don't offer again" turns this off.
rigtune.settings.mod_files.tooltip: Your launcher keeps its own list of this instance's mods. When RigTune adds, updates or disables mod files, that list goes out of date: in the Modrinth App, Update and Update all can fail until you fix it in the app; in Prism, its own update can delete files RigTune kept for Undo.
rigtune.settings.mod_files.tooltip.pendi: RigTune is still checking which launcher manages this instance's mods. If that launcher keeps its own list of them, RigTune adding, updating or disabling mod files puts that list out of date.
rigtune.settings.modrinth.tooltip: Sends the SHA-1 hashes of your mod jars and the ids of mods RigTune might suggest (to find updates and check availability), and downloads the mods you choose to install. Off: installs and updates become advice for your launcher.
rigtune.settings.network.tooltip: Off: RigTune makes no network request at all. No rules updates, no Modrinth lookups, update checks or downloads.
rigtune.settings.note: RigTune has no telemetry. Hover a switch to see what it sends.
rigtune.settings.privacy_toast.body: Only for rules and Modrinth, no telemetry. Turn it off in RigTune's Settings.
rigtune.settings.privacy_toast.title: RigTune uses the network
rigtune.settings.remote_rules.tooltip: Downloads the latest recommendation rules from RigTune's GitHub repository. Nothing about you is sent. Off: the rules in the jar (or the last download) are used.
rigtune.settings.scene.tooltip: Where the benchmark runs: your current position, or RigTune's own benchmark world (the same scene every time).
rigtune.settings.startup_toast.tooltip: The "RigTune: N suggestions" toast on the title screen. Apply results and warnings are always shown.
rigtune.settings.title: RigTune settings
rigtune.share.copied: Copied the report to the clipboard (%s characters).
rigtune.share.unavailable: Nothing to copy yet: the report is still being built.
rigtune.server.cap_reason: The server sends at most %s chunks.
rigtune.server.detail.changed: This server's limit changed since last time (was %s).
rigtune.server.detail.dh: Distant Horizons may still show terrain you've already explored beyond it; generating new distant terrain may need Distant Horizons on the server.
rigtune.server.detail.simulation: Simulation distance on this server: %s chunks (the server decides it).
rigtune.server.detail.you_set: You set %1$s; the server sends %2$s, so %2$s is what you see.
rigtune.server.notice: The server limits view distance to %s chunks
rigtune.server.notice.you_set: The server limits view distance to %s chunks (you set %s)
rigtune.awareness.driver_changed: Your GPU driver changed since last time (%s → %s)
rigtune.awareness.gpu_changed: Your GPU changed since last time
rigtune.awareness.hardware_changed: Your hardware changed since last time
rigtune.awareness.hardware_changed.detai: Re-scan to refresh the recommendations, or re-benchmark to measure again.
rigtune.awareness.whats_new.many: %s new recommendations for you since you last looked: %s, +%s more
rigtune.awareness.whats_new.one: 1 new recommendation for you since you last looked: %s
rigtune.outside.changed.many: %s settings were changed outside the game since you last played (e.g. %s).
rigtune.outside.changed.one: A setting was changed outside the game since you last played (%s).
rigtune.outside.detail: Changed: %s. "Apply RigTune's values again" sets RigTune's values back as one History entry you can undo; Keep leaves them.
rigtune.outside.detail.modrinth_app: The Modrinth App's game-settings sync can do this. To stop it: App settings → Synced settings → Sync game options, or this instance → Instance settings → Sync overrides → Unsync game settings.
rigtune.outside.reason: RigTune's value before it was changed outside the game.
rigtune.outside.sync_line: If the Modrinth App syncs game settings, it copies these to your other synced instances.
rigtune.outside.toast.title: Settings changed outside the game
rigtune.header.tier_basis.cpu.fallback_c: CPU tier %s (fallback estimate from %s threads at %s GHz)
rigtune.header.tier_basis.cpu.fallback_u: CPU tier %s (fallback estimate; the thread count is unknown)
rigtune.firstrun.applied.downloading: Mod downloads are still running; the ones that finish are added to this list.
rigtune.firstrun.applied.no_mod_files: This Apply didn't change any mod files.
rigtune.firstrun.applied.no_restart: Everything listed here is in effect now. No restart needed.
rigtune.firstrun.applied.nothing: Nothing was recorded for this Apply.
rigtune.firstrun.applied.restart: Restart Minecraft to finish: RigTune makes the changes waiting for a restart after you close the game.
rigtune.firstrun.applied.title: Your first Apply
rigtune.firstrun.applied.undo.tooltip: See exactly what would be put back, then confirm.
rigtune.firstrun.applied.undo_hint: Changed your mind? Undo this Apply shows what it would put back before it changes anything. History… keeps this list for later.
rigtune.firstrun.how.mods: Mods are downloaded when you press Apply and added at the next restart. A mod RigTune turns off is renamed to .jar.disabled, never deleted.
rigtune.firstrun.how.now: Minecraft's own settings change as soon as you press Apply.
rigtune.firstrun.how.preview: Preview shows every change, file by file, before anything happens.
rigtune.firstrun.how.restart: Sodium, Distant Horizons and Iris settings are written after you close Minecraft, and take effect the next time it starts.
rigtune.firstrun.how.ticked: Nothing changes until you press Apply, and only the ticked items change, with any mods they need. Untick anything you don't want.
rigtune.firstrun.how.ticked.settings: Nothing changes until you press Apply, and only the ticked settings change. Untick anything you don't want.
rigtune.firstrun.how.title: How Apply works
rigtune.firstrun.how.undo: History… lists everything RigTune changed. Undo this puts back one Apply, Undo last the most recent one, and Undo all everything; each shows what it will put back first.
rigtune.firstrun.notice: New? History… lets you undo each Apply.
rigtune.firstrun.notice.detail: Only the ticked items change, with any mods they need. Game settings change when you press Apply; Sodium, Distant Horizons and Iris settings and mod changes take effect at the next restart. Preview shows each change first.
rigtune.firstrun.notice.detail.settings: Only the ticked settings change. Game settings change when you press Apply; Sodium, Distant Horizons and Iris settings at the next restart. Preview shows each change first.
rigtune.notice.open.tooltip: This notice's options, and any other notices
rigtune.notice.title: Notices
rigtune.launcher.jvm_steps.atlauncher: this instance's Settings button → Java/Minecraft → Java Parameters.
rigtune.launcher.jvm_steps.curseforge: My Modpacks → this pack's three-dot menu → Profile Options → Advanced Settings → Additional Arguments, and Settings (gear icon) → Minecraft → Default Additional Arguments.
rigtune.launcher.jvm_steps.gdlauncher: this instance → Settings tab → Instance Java Arguments, and Settings (gear icon) → Java → Java Arguments.
rigtune.launcher.jvm_steps.modrinth_app: this instance → Instance settings (gear) → Sync overrides → turn on Custom Java arguments → edit the box.
rigtune.launcher.jvm_steps.multimc: right-click this instance → Edit Instance → Settings → Java → tick Java arguments → edit the box.
rigtune.launcher.jvm_steps.official: Installations → select this installation → More Options → JVM Arguments, then Save.
rigtune.launcher.jvm_steps.prism: right-click this instance → Edit... → Settings → Java → tick Java Arguments → edit the box.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.guide: This instance's mods are managed by %s: RigTune changes settings only.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.news: RigTune now leaves this instance's mod files to %s
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.news.detail: Installing, updating and turning off mods now come with the launcher's own steps. Settings → Mod files lets RigTune change them anyway.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.news.detail.u: Installing, updating and turning off mods are now left to your launcher. Settings → Mod files lets RigTune change them anyway.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.note.add: This instance's mods are managed by %s: install it there.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.note.disable: This instance's mods are managed by %s: turn it off there.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.note.pending: Checking which launcher manages this instance's mods; mod changes wait until then.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.note.update: This instance's mods are managed by %s: update it there.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.opted_in: RigTune changes mod files here; %s's own list may go out of date.
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.preview: Mod changes to make in %s: %s (listed on the main screen)
rigtune.launcher.mod_files.preview.pendi: Mod changes waiting until RigTune knows which launcher manages this instance's mods: %s (listed on the main screen)
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.atlauncher.ad: this instance's Edit Mods button → Browse Mods.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.atlauncher.di: this instance's Edit Mods button → select it → Disable Selected.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.atlauncher.en: this instance's Edit Mods button → select it → Enable Selected.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.atlauncher.up: this instance's Edit Mods button → select it → Check For Updates.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.curseforge.ad: My Modpacks → this pack → add it to the pack's content (Profile Options → Allow content management for this profile must be ticked).
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.curseforge.di: My Modpacks → this pack → Content → switch it off (Profile Options → Allow content management for this profile must be ticked).
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.curseforge.en: My Modpacks → this pack → Content → switch it on.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.curseforge.up: My Modpacks → this pack → Content → right-click it → Update.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.gdlauncher.di: this instance → Mods → select it → Disable Mod.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.gdlauncher.en: this instance → Mods → select it → Enable.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.gdlauncher.up: this instance → Mods → select it → Update (or Update All Mods).
this instance → Content → Browse content, then install it there.
this instance → Content → select it → Disable.
this instance → Content → filter Disabled → select it → Enable.
update RigTune in this instance's Content tab, or download it and use Content → Upload files, then delete the old RigTune there.
this instance → Content → select it → Update (or Update all).
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.multimc.add: right-click this instance → Edit Instance → Loader mods → Add, and pick the downloaded jar.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.multimc.disab: right-click this instance → Edit Instance → Loader mods → select it → Disable.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.multimc.enabl: right-click this instance → Edit Instance → Loader mods → select it → Enable.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.multimc.updat: right-click this instance → Edit Instance → Loader mods → Remove the old version, then Add the new jar.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.prism.add: right-click this instance → Edit... → Mods → Download Mods.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.prism.disable: right-click this instance → Edit... → Mods → select it → Disable.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.prism.enable: right-click this instance → Edit... → Mods → select it → Enable.
rigtune.launcher.mod_steps.prism.update: right-click this instance → Edit... → Mods → select it → Check for Updates.
rigtune.launcher.steps.atlauncher: this instance's Settings button → Java/Minecraft → Maximum Memory/Ram.
rigtune.launcher.steps.curseforge.global: Settings (gear icon) → Minecraft → Java Settings → Allocated Memory.
rigtune.launcher.steps.curseforge.pack: My Modpacks → this pack's three-dot menu → Profile Options → Memory Settings → choose Custom RAM Allocation → set the slider.
rigtune.launcher.steps.gdlauncher: this instance → Settings tab → turn on Instance Java Memory → set the slider.
rigtune.launcher.steps.modrinth_app: this instance → Instance settings (gear) → Sync overrides → turn on Custom memory allocation → set the slider.
rigtune.launcher.steps.multimc: right-click this instance → Edit Instance → Settings → Java → tick Memory → Maximum memory allocation.
rigtune.launcher.steps.official: Installations → select this installation → More Options → JVM Arguments: change the number in -Xmx (-Xmx4G is 4 GB), then Save.
rigtune.launcher.steps.prism: right-click this instance → Edit... → Settings → Java → tick Memory → Maximum Memory Usage.
rigtune.launcher.xmx_in_java_args: Your Java arguments also contain -Xmx, which %s uses instead of the memory slider: change or remove it there.
rigtune.jvm.advice_loading: RigTune is still working out its advice.
rigtune.jvm.finding.explicit_gc_disabled: stops Minecraft's out-of-memory recovery and Java's direct-memory cleanup from asking for a collection, with no benefit in play
rigtune.jvm.finding.ignored: this Java doesn't have this option and ignores it (a future Java may refuse to start with it)
rigtune.jvm.finding.no_gc: a collector that never frees memory: the game runs out of memory and crashes
rigtune.jvm.finding.overridden: this Java doesn't accept this setting here and uses its own value
rigtune.jvm.finding.server_set: part of Paper's server flags (Aikar's flags) or a set based on them
rigtune.jvm.finding.stop_the_world_gc: a collector Java's documentation describes for work where long pauses are acceptable
rigtune.jvm.finding.xmx_duplicate: set more than once; Java uses the last one
rigtune.jvm.finding.young_gen_fixed: fixes the young generation's size, which turns off G1's pause-time control (Java's documentation)
rigtune.jvm.no_advice: No Java or memory advice for this PC.
rigtune.jvm.no_findings: Nothing to note about your Java arguments.
rigtune.jvm.subtitle: RigTune never suggests adding GC flags.
rigtune.jvm.title: JVM & memory
rigtune.jvm.unavailable: RigTune can't check the Java arguments on this Java (it needs a HotSpot-based Java such as Temurin or Zulu).
rigtune.download.breaks_version_batch: %s doesn't work with %s %s, which would be installed too
rigtune.download.breaks_version_staged: %s doesn't work with %s %s, which is waiting for a restart
rigtune.download.conflicts: it conflicts with %s, which is ticked too; tick only one of them
rigtune.download.incompatible: Modrinth marks %s as incompatible with %s, which is installed
rigtune.download.incompatible_both: Modrinth marks %s and %s as incompatible, and both would be installed
rigtune.download.incompatible_installed: Modrinth marks %s, which is installed, as incompatible with %s
rigtune.download.incompatible_staged: Modrinth marks %s as incompatible with %s, which is waiting for a restart
rigtune.download.missing_dependency: its new version needs %s, which isn't installed
rigtune.download.missing_dependency_stag: its new version needs %s, which is waiting for a restart; update it after restarting
rigtune.download.needs_disabled: it needs %s, which is being turned off at the next restart
rigtune.download.needs_version_batch: %s needs %s %s, not the %s that would be installed too
rigtune.download.needs_version_staged: %s needs %s %s, not the %s that's waiting for a restart
rigtune.download.not_a_mod: %s is not a Fabric mod jar (no readable fabric.mod.json id)

rigtune.download.outside_mods_folder: it isn't in this instance's mods folder; update it in your launcher
rigtune.download.pinned_batch: %s, which would be installed too, needs %s %s, not %s
rigtune.download.pinned_breaks: %s, which is installed, doesn't work with %s %s
rigtune.download.pinned_breaks_batch: %s, which would be installed too, doesn't work with %s %s
rigtune.download.pinned_breaks_staged: %s, which is waiting for a restart, doesn't work with %s %s
rigtune.download.pinned_staged: %s, which is waiting for a restart, needs %s %s, not %s
rigtune.download.staged_incompatible: Modrinth marks %s, which is waiting for a restart, as incompatible with %s
rigtune.download.stale: its Modrinth data changed since the list was made; try again
rigtune.download.target_exists: %s is already in the mods folder
rigtune.a11y.row.select: Press Enter or Space to select
rigtune.startup.advice: Fewer mods and an SSD help launch time most. If it jumped after you added a mod, check that mod first.
rigtune.startup.perf_counters.link.entry: Microsoft's registry reference, "Disable Performance Counters Entry": %s
rigtune.startup.perf_counters.link.kb: Microsoft's KB 2554336, whose first step is checking this setting: %s
rigtune.startup.perf_counters.measured: Minecraft's crash-report setup took %s s at this launch; about 1 s is usual. It asks Windows for these counters, so part of that time may be related to this setting.
rigtune.startup.perf_counters.off: Windows performance counters are turned off on this PC. "Disable Performance Counters" is Windows' own Perflib setting; it turns off every registry-based performance counter on the PC.
rigtune.startup.perf_counters.windows: 0 is Windows' default. Changing it needs an administrator and a Windows restart, and a tuning tool may have set it on purpose. RigTune doesn't change Windows settings.
rigtune.startup.last_median: Last launch %s s · median of the last %s: %s s
rigtune.startup.mod_set_changed: The mod set changed since the previous launch (may be related).
rigtune.toast.title: RigTune: %s suggestions
rigtune.toast.body: Press %s or open RigTune to review
rigtune.history.corrupt: config/rigtune/history.json can't be read, so there's nothing to show. RigTune keeps a copy of it (history.json.bad) when it next writes the history.
rigtune.history.error: Could not read RigTune's history; see the log.
rigtune.history.failed: Last attempt failed: %s (try %s of %s at restart)
rigtune.history.failed_held: Can't finish on its own yet; RigTune tries again at each exit (see config/rigtune/helper.log)
rigtune.history.newer: config/rigtune/history.json was written by a newer RigTune, so this version can't show or change it.
rigtune.history.not_applied_dropped: Not applied: dropped before it could run (for example, the mod was installed another way)
rigtune.history.open.tooltip: What RigTune changed, newest first. Undo one entry, the last apply or everything from there.
rigtune.history.subtitle: Newest first · select an entry to see its changes
rigtune.history.title: What RigTune changed
rigtune.history.undo.subtitle: One entry of the history
rigtune.history.undo_this.tooltip: Revert the selected entry's changes that nothing has changed since. You see exactly what changes before anything happens.
rigtune.tools.open.tooltip: Benchmark, Profiles, Stutter Doctor, JVM & memory and your benchmark history.
rigtune.tools.title: Tools
rigtune.tryit.action.cancel.tooltip: Undoes the change (History's Undo this) and ends this Try it.
rigtune.tryit.action.keep.tooltip: Keeps the change and ends this Try it. Only RigTune's own Try it record is written.
rigtune.tryit.action.revert.tooltip: Opens Undo this for the change. Settings go back now; Sodium, Distant Horizons and Iris settings at the next restart.
rigtune.tryit.button.tooltip: Measures now, applies this change, measures again, then lets you keep or revert it.
rigtune.tryit.cause.fresh_world: the first run in a new benchmark world
rigtune.tryit.caveat.dh: Distant Horizons builds distant terrain in the background, which can make runs vary.
rigtune.tryit.caveat.noisy: These runs varied a lot (more than 5%%), so the result is less certain.
rigtune.tryit.caveat.scene: A measured comparison in one scene, not proof: busier places may differ.
rigtune.tryit.caveat.sessions: The two measurements were in different game sessions: a driver or background program change would show up here too.
rigtune.tryit.caveat.world_content: The benchmark world has no mobs and clear weather, so this setting may show little change there.
rigtune.tryit.duration.restart: This setting takes effect at the next start: measure now, restart Minecraft, then measure again (about a minute each).
rigtune.tryit.intro: RigTune measures your game now, applies this change, and measures again in the same place. Then you choose: keep it or revert it.
rigtune.tryit.notice.ended: Try it: your try of %s has ended. Open it to see how.
rigtune.tryit.notice.history: Try it: History can't be read right now, so your try of %s waits.
rigtune.tryit.notice.ready: Try it: %s is in effect. Measure again to see what it did.
rigtune.tryit.notice.result: Try it: your result for %s is ready.
rigtune.tryit.notice.waiting: Try it: %s is waiting for a restart.
rigtune.tryit.overlay.between: Try it: first measurement done. Applying the change and measuring again…
rigtune.tryit.refused.history: History can't be written right now, so this change couldn't be reverted.
rigtune.tryit.refused.kind: Only settings can be tried; mod changes can't.
rigtune.tryit.refused.no_file: This setting's config file wasn't found.
rigtune.tryit.refused.one: Tick exactly one suggestion to try it.
rigtune.tryit.refused.open: Finish or cancel your other Try it first (%s).
rigtune.tryit.refused.pending: Other changes are waiting for a restart. Restart (or Discard them) first, so only this change is measured.
rigtune.tryit.refused.preset: This setting changes many others at once, so it can't be tried on its own.
rigtune.tryit.refused.remote_sd: On a server, the server decides the simulation distance.
rigtune.tryit.refused.running: A Try it (measured) is still in progress. Finish or cancel it first.
rigtune.tryit.refused.storage: Results can't be saved right now; see the log.
rigtune.tryit.refused.unmeasurable: Benchmarks always run with the frame rate uncapped, so this setting can't be measured.
rigtune.tryit.refused.unsupported: RigTune doesn't change this setting, so it can't be tried.
rigtune.tryit.scene.current: Measured here, where you stand. The screen and controls are taken over while it measures; Esc stops it.
rigtune.tryit.scene.world: Measured in the benchmark world: same spot, time and weather every time.
rigtune.tryit.stage.cancelled: Cancelled: the change was taken back before it was applied. Nothing was changed.
rigtune.tryit.stage.entry_missing: History no longer lists this change, so RigTune can't tell whether it's in effect or revert it from here.
rigtune.tryit.stage.history_unreadable: History can't be read right now, so this Try it waits. Try again in a moment.
rigtune.tryit.stage.interrupted: No verdict: the game restarted between the two measurements in your own world, so they can't be matched.
rigtune.tryit.stage.no_before: No verdict: the first measurement is no longer in the benchmark history.
rigtune.tryit.stage.no_entry: History folded this change into an older entry, so it can't be reverted from here. It stays applied.
rigtune.tryit.stage.not_applied: The change wasn't applied (%s), so there's nothing to measure or revert.
rigtune.tryit.stage.ready: The change is in effect. Measure again to see what it did.
rigtune.tryit.stage.ready.world: Measure again from the title screen: the benchmark world opens from there.
rigtune.tryit.stage.restart: Quit and restart Minecraft. RigTune reminds you to measure again at the next start.
rigtune.tryit.stage.retrying: The change wasn't applied at the last restart (%s). RigTune tries again at the next restart (try %s of 3).
rigtune.tryit.stage.revert_pending: Reverted: %s gets its old value at the next restart.
rigtune.tryit.stage.stopped_after: Stopped before the second measurement. The change is applied.
